newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar gently firmer but trade thin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar gently firmer but trade thin.

text.p: White sugar futures edged higher in listless Thursday activity as trade players were content to remain sidelined and funds were reluctant to increase their long position, market sources said.
Spot October accounted for the bulk of the thin turnover but much of this came in the form of Oct/March spread trading, with little interest seen in the second-month December contract.
The position traditionally attracts relatively little interest as there is no equivalent position in New York for arbitrage trading.
October/October did draw some interest, narrowing to around $71 from the $72.50 at the start of the week.
"For the time being people are looking to come in and sell -- if it breaks $70.00 I think there'll be more selling," said one trader.
At 1620 GMT all positions were slightly firmer. October was up 80 cents at $328.50 and December up 60 cents at $323.40. Volume amounted to 478 lots.
Market sources said fund players in London were content to wait for another burst of sentiment before returning to the market as they had already increased their long positions.
"There aren't many fund stops around on the upside because the funds have got their long positions in and they're not bothered," the trader said.
The Paris market was exceedingly quiet with four lots traded. October was up 50 cents at $328.00 and December up 90 cents at $323.40.
